svg.text: R0 Low-Level Design — how services talk, and when data is stored
Not the HLD. The HLD (r0-reference-architecture.svg) is the ten-boundary picture. This file is the runtime LLD: numbered hops, writes, stores.
Rendering of docs/architecture/R0-LLD.md · owns nothing (HA-02) · SUG-20260820-lf2 · AI-DRAFTED — T4 Architecture / Security / Database / SRE outstanding
1 One RM click — the north-south hops, and what is stored at the BFF. 2 Who is allowed to call whom (east-west). 3 The sale, step by step — actor, seam, WRITE, store, sync/async.
4 Special paths that skip the happy path (C4 payment, quote poll, outbox). 5 Compact AWS placement — where those hops sit. Colour in fig 5 is trust zone, not build wave.
green WRITE = a row is persisted now
One RM / IPR request — numbered hops. Domain writes (hop 8) wait for PDP ALLOW (hop 6).
Every click: Flutter → CloudFront → WAF → API Gateway (external reverse proxy) → internal ALB → #2 BFF → PDP, then a domain service. Flutter never receives OAuth tokens.
Hops 1–5 store nothing about the sale. Hop 6 is authorization, not persistence. The first business write is hop 8, and only after ALLOW.
Who may call whom — east-west. If an arrow is not drawn, the call is forbidden.
Flutter talks only to #2. #2 never talks to Hub or 1SB. Life cell (#10/#11) reaches 1SB only through Hub → Adapter. Customer never calls the platform.
Payment URL is sent to the customer. It is never returned into the RM session (FF-14 / C4).
EDGE ns:edge — the only public target
DOMAIN — BFF may call these. They are cluster-private. They are not on API Gateway.
BFF → #5 and #9 directly. Other domains: #9 orchestrates (stage + refs only, SC-W3-6).
LIFE CELL ns:life-cell then INTEGRATION ns:integration then OUTSIDE
LOB-owned execution — first physical split seam (not now)
egress via NAT EIP · we poll
FORBIDDEN Flutter → domain service · BFF → Hub / 1SB · 1SB inbound webhook · RM session ← payment URL · cross-schema SQL · Kafka / shared Redis
The sale — who talks, what is written, where it lands, when. This is the persistence LLD.
#9 holds stage and references only (SC-W3-6). Each WRITE is in the owning context’s store. No service reads another’s tables. No Kafka.
Opaque session. OAuth tokens stay in BFF.
Opportunity + accountable SP + lob. RM only.
Customer snapshot. CBS is not written.
Sync. Hold INITIATED if CBS fails.
Stage + external refs only. No copied decisions.
Assessment (C1). Quote is illegal without it.
Sync grant. Cannot advance without it (C2).
Sync. Fail closed. No compiled default.
Quote row + job. Raw provider payload.
Aurora quotation · DDB jobs · S3 raw
Async-poll. NO automatic retry on submit.
Payment session. Link goes to customer, not RM.
Nothing in our VPC. 3-D Secure on PG page.
Batch. Money path recovers by recon, not DB restore.
Three paths that are not the hop-1–8 happy path — payment C4, quote async-poll, outbox.
If you only remember three LLD rules: customer pays outside our VPC; quote submit is not retried; audit is async but SOLD waits for it.
RM session creates a payment. The URL is sent to the customer. RM never sees it.
Callback S-14 · separate API Gateway route
IP-allowlisted to PG · signature verified in #12 · not on the RM cookie path
Settlement S-15 is a file/batch, not the callback. UNCERTAIN is a real state — never guessed to PAID.
#13 Policy will not issue unless payment is RECONCILED (SC-W3-4).
Policy issuance is hop 8 in figure 3. It is a re-check, not a side effect of the callback.
Quote / proposal submit is not a request-reply
Human is waiting, but 1SB is slow. We return 202 and poll. We do not retry submit.
Poll loop S-11 GET until QUOTED / PARTIALLY_QUOTED / FAILED / TIMED_OUT
PARTIAL is success. Budget exhausted → TIMED_OUT. Recover by polling the external ref — never by re-POSTing submit.
Same pattern for proposal S-12. Same job table. Same no-retry-on-submit rule.
R0 has no insurer callback API Gateway. Building one now is a public surface with no consumer.
bank-persistence-service stays the job store for #15. Do not route Opportunity / Consent / Payment through it.
A human-waiting step commits locally. Side effects go to ns:jobs workers.
S-17 audit: business commits; journey cannot reach SOLD until the four required events are acked.
S-18 notification: never blocks the journey. Lost SMS is an ops retry, not a stage rollback.
Revisit Kafka only when a third consumer class appears, outbox lags NFR-DAT-05, or #18 MIS enters at S13.
Where those hops sit on AWS — compact placement. Solid = PROVISION. Dashed grey = DO NOT PROVISION.
One VPC per environment, ap-south-1. No PVC on business pods. One Aurora cluster, schema per context (ADR-008). Kafka / shared Redis / Istio / extra proxies are out.
Call centre / branch R2 — same journey, later actor
Z1 PUBLIC EDGE (not in the VPC) = hops 1–4
VPC 10.{env}.0.0/16 · 3 AZs · hops 5–9 live here · prod does not share with uat
Public subnets — NAT + EIP only. No workloads.
1SB and PG allowlist THIS EIP. Prod: NAT per AZ.
Namespaces: edge · identity · shared-platform · life-cell · integration · jobs
Aurora · (ElastiCache only if WS-2 forces sessions)
NO PVC on business services · NO mesh (Istio/App Mesh) · HPA min 2 · Keycloak JDBC → Aurora keycloak
DO NOT PROVISION: MSK/Kafka · shared Redis · per-service RDS · public ALB · Kong/Nginx/F5 · insurer webhook GW
schemas: cfg opportunity customer consent suitability catalogue quotation proposal payment policy hub onesb identity keycloak notif
S-21 config TTL · catalogue · NOT ElastiCache
Authoritative if this picture disagrees: 03-solution-architecture-r0.md · ADR-001 · ADR-008 · R0-LLD.md. This SVG owns nothing.
HLD companion: docs/architecture/r0-reference-architecture.svg and R0-HLD.md. Do not provision from architecture-review/04 (target-state Kafka/Redis/Istio).
